title: Real shadow-root drag selection reports Selection.isCollapsed=true — probe getComposedRanges before trusting the flag
trigger: Drag-selecting text inside a shadow root produces a working selection (Selection.toString() returns the text) but every document-level inspection says collapsed — so guards like `if (selection.isCollapsed) return` silently drop real selections.
principle: When a selection lives entirely inside a shadow root, Chromium retargets the document-level Selection anchor/focus to the host boundary: `isCollapsed === true`, `rangeCount === 1`, and `getRangeAt(0)` is a collapsed range at the host — while `toString()` still returns the selected text. The real ranges only exist on `Selection.getComposedRanges({ shadowRoots })` (Chrome 137+, pass the roots you care about). Each returned StaticRange has no geometry APIs — rebuild a real `Range` via `document.createRange()` + `setStart/setEnd` before calling `getClientRects`/`intersectsNode`. Order matters: probe composed ranges FIRST, and only trust `isCollapsed` when no shadow roots were supplied. Test trap: `selection.addRange()` in tests creates a normal non-collapsed selection, so programmatic-selection tests pass while real mouse drag fails — reproduce with real mouse events or explicitly mock the collapsed-document + composed-range shape.

cases.context: extractTermsFromSelection() bails on `selection.isCollapsed` before checking composed ranges. Real drag-select inside the split-view subtitle panel's shadow root returns [] → bulk status keys 1-4 do nothing, while the e2e spec (which uses `selection.addRange()` programmatically) stays green.

applyFor: Any code that reads window.getSelection() where selectable text lives inside a shadow root (extension UIs, editor surfaces)
Early-exit guards on Selection.isCollapsed / rangeCount before composed-range extraction
Writing e2e/unit tests for shadow-DOM text selection — programmatic addRange() does NOT reproduce real drag selection shape
